1-nephi-1.summary: Nephi, a son of Lehi, begins his record in Jerusalem. His father, Lehi, prays and sees God in a vision. Lehi reads a heavenly book about Jerusalem's destruction. He warns the people and speaks of a coming Messiah. Some people in Jerusalem seek to kill him.

verse.text: For it came to pass in the commencement of the first year of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, (my father, Lehi, having dwelt at Jerusalem in all his days); and in that same year there came many prophets, prophesying unto the people that they must repent, or the great city Jerusalem must be destroyed.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-2.summary: The Lord tells Lehi to leave Jerusalem. Lehi takes his family into the wilderness. Laman and Lemuel, Nephi's older brothers, complain. Nephi prays and seeks God's help. The Lord promises Nephi a land if he obeys.

verse.text: Now this he spake because of the stiffneckedness of Laman and Lemuel; for behold they did murmur in many things against their father, because he was a visionary man, and had led them out of the land of Jerusalem, to leave the land of their inheritance, and their gold, and their silver, and their precious things, to perish in the wilderness. And this they said he had done because of the foolish imaginations of his heart.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lehi’s family leaves Jerusalem
routes.text: The Lord told Lehi to leave Jerusalem. The family camped three days past the Red Sea borders.
routes.note: The road down the Arabah valley is one common proposal. The text names no road.

1-nephi-3.summary: Lehi sends his sons back to Jerusalem for a set of brass plates. Laban, a powerful man in the city, keeps those plates. Laban refuses their request and takes their property. Laman and Lemuel strike their younger brothers. An angel tells them to return.

verse.text: And it came to pass that he spake unto me, saying: Behold I have dreamed a dream, in the which the Lord hath commanded me that thou and thy brethren shall return to Jerusalem.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons return for the brass plates
routes.text: Nephi and his brothers went up to Jerusalem for the plates. They came back with the plates and Zoram.

1-nephi-4.summary: Nephi enters Jerusalem and finds Laban drunk. The Spirit tells him to kill Laban. He takes the plates with help from Laban's servant, Zoram. Zoram agrees to join the family.

verse.text: And it came to pass that I spake unto my brethren, saying: Let us go up again unto Jerusalem, and let us be faithful in keeping the commandments of the Lord; for behold he is mightier than all the earth, then why not mightier than Laban and his fifty, yea, or even than his tens of thousands?
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons return for the brass plates
routes.text: Nephi and his brothers went up to Jerusalem for the plates. They came back with the plates and Zoram.

1-nephi-5.summary: Sariah, Lehi's wife, fears that her sons have died. Their return strengthens her trust in the Lord. Lehi reads the brass plates and learns his family line. The family keeps the records for its journey.

verse.text: And it had come to pass that my father spake unto her, saying: I know that I am a visionary man; for if I had not seen the things of God in a vision I should not have known the goodness of God, but had tarried at Jerusalem, and had perished with my brethren.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-6.summary: Nephi explains the purpose of his record. He leaves out his family's full genealogy. He wants readers to come to God and be saved. He tells later writers to preserve things of worth.

verse.text: And now I, Nephi, do not give the genealogy of my fathers in this part of my record; neither at any time shall I give it after upon these plates which I am writing; for it is given in the record which has been kept by my father; wherefore, I do not write it in this work.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-7.summary: Lehi sends his sons back for the family of Ishmael, a man in Jerusalem. Ishmael's daughters will become the sons' wives. Some rebel on the journey back. Nephi escapes the ropes that bind him. The families return to Lehi and give thanks.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the Lord commanded him that I, Nephi, and my brethren, should again return unto the land of Jerusalem, and bring down Ishmael and his family into the wilderness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons bring Ishmael’s family
routes.text: The sons went up to Jerusalem again. Ishmael’s family came down with them to the valley.

1-nephi-8.summary: Lehi describes a tree with desirable fruit. He invites his family to eat it. People follow an iron rod, lose their way, or mock others. Lehi urges Laman and Lemuel to obey the Lord.

verse.text: And it came to pass that we had gathered together all manner of seeds of every kind, both of grain of every kind, and also of the seeds of fruit of every kind.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-9.summary: Nephi describes two sets of records. One holds the history of kings and wars. The other gives more space to religious teaching. He trusts the Lord's purpose for both.

verse.text: And all these things did my father see, and hear, and speak, as he dwelt in a tent, in the valley of Lemuel, and also a great many more things, which cannot be written upon these plates.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-10.summary: Lehi foretells Jerusalem's fall and the coming Messiah. He describes a prophet who will baptize the Messiah. He compares scattered Israel to broken olive branches. Nephi wants to learn these things for himself.

verse.text: That after they should be destroyed, even that great city Jerusalem, and many be carried away captive into Babylon, according to the own due time of the Lord, they should return again, yea, even be brought back out of captivity; and after they should be brought back out of captivity they should possess again the land of their inheritance.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-11.summary: The Spirit shows Nephi the tree from Lehi's dream. An angel shows him Mary and the Son of God. Nephi sees Christ's ministry, baptism, and death. He learns that the great building represents the world's pride.

verse.text: And it came to pass that I looked and beheld the great city of Jerusalem, and also other cities. And I beheld the city of Nazareth; and in the city of Nazareth I beheld a virgin, and she was exceedingly fair and white.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-12.summary: Nephi sees wars among his descendants. He sees destruction before Christ visits the survivors. Generations live in peace before pride and war return. His people's destruction follows.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the angel said unto me: Look, and behold thy seed, and also the seed of thy brethren. And I looked and beheld the land of promise; and I beheld multitudes of people, yea, even as it were in number as many as the sand of the sea.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-13.summary: Nephi sees nations beyond the promised land. He sees people cross the sea and receive a book. An angel describes truths lost from that record. Other records will make the Lamb's teachings known.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the angel spake unto me, saying: Look! And I looked and beheld many nations and kingdoms.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-14.summary: An angel describes the choices facing the Gentiles. He shows Nephi two opposing churches. God's covenant people receive power despite their small numbers. Nephi leaves part of the vision for another writer.

verse.text: And it shall come to pass, that if the Gentiles shall hearken unto the Lamb of God in that day that he shall manifest himself unto them in word, and also in power, in very deed, unto the taking away of their stumbling blocks—
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-15.summary: Nephi finds his brothers disputing Lehi's words. He explains Israel's scattering and later gathering. He identifies the iron rod as God's word. He also explains the river and final judgment.

verse.text: And it came to pass that after I, Nephi, had been carried away in the Spirit, and seen all these things, I returned to the tent of my father.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

1-nephi-16.summary: The families marry and receive a guiding instrument. Nephi's broken bow leaves them without food. He makes another bow and asks where to hunt. Ishmael dies, and further complaints lead to the Lord's correction.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the daughters of Ishmael did mourn exceedingly, because of the loss of their father, and because of their afflictions in the wilderness; and they did murmur against my father, because he had brought them out of the land of Jerusalem, saying: Our father is dead; yea, and we have wandered much in the wilderness, and we have suffered much affliction, hunger, thirst, and fatigue; and after all these sufferings we must perish in the wilderness with hunger.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: From the valley to Nahom
routes.text: The family traveled south-southeast near the Red Sea. Nephi’s bow broke on the way. Ishmael died at Nahom.
routes.note: Researchers follow the old incense road east of the coastal mountains. The text names only Shazer and Nahom.

1-nephi-17.summary: The family reaches a coast called Bountiful. The Lord tells Nephi to build a ship. His brothers mock him, and he recalls God's help to Moses. God's power shakes them when they oppose Nephi.

verse.text: Yea, and the Lord said also that: After ye have arrived in the promised land, ye shall know that I, the Lord, am God; and that I, the Lord, did deliver you from destruction; yea, that I did bring you out of the land of Jerusalem.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Eastward to Bountiful
routes.text: From Nahom the family traveled nearly eastward. After eight years in the wilderness they reached the sea.
routes.note: This line runs along the south edge of the great Arabian desert. The stops are not known.

1-nephi-18.summary: The family finishes the ship and sails. Nephi's brothers bind him during the voyage. A storm ends after they release him. They reach the promised land and begin to plant crops.

verse.text: And it came to pass that they did worship the Lord, and did go forth with me; and we did work timbers of curious workmanship. And the Lord did show me from time to time after what manner I should work the timbers of the ship.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lehi’s family reaches the promised land
routes.text: The ship crossed the sea and arrived at the promised land.

2-nephi-5.summary: Nephi leaves his brothers because they seek his life. His followers settle in a land they call Nephi. They build a temple and work the land. Nephi describes their records, worship, and later conflicts.

verse.text: Behold, it came to pass that I, Nephi, did cry much unto the Lord my God, because of the anger of my brethren.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Nephi’s people move to the land of Nephi
routes.text: Nephi’s people fled into the wilderness for many days. They called the new place Nephi.

omni-1.summary: Five descendants of Jacob keep the small plates in turn. They are Omni, Amaron, Chemish, Abinadom, and Amaleki. Amaleki, the last of them, tells how Mosiah leads faithful Nephites north. They find the city of Zarahemla and a people who left Jerusalem with Mulek. Mosiah becomes king of both peoples and reads a stone from an earlier people. Amaleki gives the plates to King Benjamin, Mosiah's son.

verse.text: Behold, I am Amaleki, the son of Abinadom. Behold, I will speak unto you somewhat concerning Mosiah, who was made king over the land of Zarahemla; for behold, he being warned of the Lord that he should flee out of the land of Nephi, and as many as would hearken unto the voice of the Lord should also depart out of the land with him, into the wilderness—
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla cross the sea
routes.text: The Lord brought Mulek’s people across the great waters into the land north.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla go up the Sidon
routes.text: They came from the place of landing up into the south wilderness.

routes.title: Mosiah leads his people down to Zarahemla
routes.text: Mosiah fled out of the land of Nephi and came down into Zarahemla.

routes.title: Zeniff’s people go up to Nephi
routes.text: A group went up into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi.

words-of-mormon-1.summary: Mormon, a later prophet, makes a shorter record from many Nephite records. He finds Nephi's small plates and joins them to his record. He recalls King Benjamin's battles and the work of prophets. Their efforts restore peace among the people.

verse.text: And it came to pass also that the armies of the Lamanites came down out of the land of Nephi, to battle against his people. But behold, king Benjamin gathered together his armies, and he did stand against them; and he did fight with the strength of his own arm, with the sword of Laban.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-1.summary: King Benjamin, the Nephite king in Zarahemla, teaches his sons from the preserved records. He explains why those records matter. He chooses his son Mosiah, named after Benjamin's father, as the next king. Mosiah calls the people together to hear Benjamin.

verse.text: And now there was no more contention in all the land of Zarahemla, among all the people who belonged to king Benjamin, so that king Benjamin had continual peace all the remainder of his days.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-2.summary: Benjamin addresses families gathered near the temple. He recalls serving them without seeking wealth. He teaches that service to others serves God. He warns against rebellion and urges obedience.

verse.text: And also that they might give thanks to the Lord their God, who had brought them out of the land of Jerusalem, and who had delivered them out of the hands of their enemies, and had appointed just men to be their teachers, and also a just man to be their king, who had established peace in the land of Zarahemla, and who had taught them to keep the commandments of God, that they might rejoice and be filled with love towards God and all men.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-7.summary: Years earlier, a man named Zeniff led a group back to the land of Nephi. King Mosiah sends sixteen men to find Zeniff's people. Ammon, a strong man of Zarahemla, leads the search. He reaches Shilom and meets King Limhi, Zeniff's grandson. Limhi learns that Zarahemla still exists. He urges his people to trust God.

verse.text: And now, it came to pass that after king Mosiah had had continual peace for the space of three years, he was desirous to know concerning the people who went up to dwell in the land of Lehi-Nephi, or in the city of Lehi-Nephi; for his people had heard nothing from them from the time they left the land of Zarahemla; therefore, they wearied him with their teasings.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Ammon’s men search for Zeniff’s people
routes.text: Sixteen men wandered forty days. They did not know the way up.

mosiah-8.summary: Ammon teaches Limhi's people. Limhi describes a search party that found ruins and metal plates. He asks whether someone can read them. Ammon explains that King Mosiah is a seer who can translate them.

verse.text: And it came to pass that after king Limhi had made an end of speaking to his people, for he spake many things unto them and only a few of them have I written in this book, he told his people all the things concerning their brethren who were in the land of Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Limhi’s explorers miss Zarahemla
routes.text: Forty-three men looked for Zarahemla. They found a land of bones and returned.

mosiah-9.summary: Zeniff, Limhi's grandfather, begins his own record. He recalls his desire to settle in the land of Nephi. King Laman, a Lamanite ruler, gives his people Nephi and Shilom. They rebuild and farm the land. They later defend themselves against a Lamanite attack.

verse.text: Therefore, I contended with my brethren in the wilderness, for I would that our ruler should make a treaty with them; but he being an austere and a blood-thirsty man commanded that I should be slain; but I was rescued by the shedding of much blood; for father fought against father, and brother against brother, until the greater number of our army was destroyed in the wilderness; and we returned, those of us that were spared, to the land of Zarahemla, to relate that tale to their wives and their children.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Zeniff’s people go up to Nephi
routes.text: A group went up into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi.

mosiah-10.summary: Zeniff prepares weapons and guards. A Lamanite army attacks after years of peace. He describes the beliefs that drive their hatred. His people prevail, and he later gives the kingdom to his son Noah.

verse.text: And it came to pass that they came up upon the north of the land of Shilom, with their numerous hosts, men armed with bows, and with arrows, and with swords, and with cimeters, and with stones, and with slings; and they had their heads shaved that they were naked; and they were girded with a leathern girdle about their loins.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-11.summary: King Noah, Zeniff's son, rules with heavy taxes and corrupt priests. He builds richly while his people become wicked. Abinadi, a prophet among them, warns that bondage will follow unless they repent. Noah and the people reject him.

verse.text: And it came to pass that he built a tower near the temple; yea, a very high tower, even so high that he could stand upon the top thereof and overlook the land of Shilom, and also the land of Shemlon, which was possessed by the Lamanites; and he could even look over all the land round about.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-18.summary: Alma secretly teaches Abinadi's words. Believers gather at Mormon, a place with a fountain of pure water. They receive baptism there. Alma organizes priests and teaches unity and care for others. The group flees after Noah discovers them.

verse.text: And it came to pass after many days there were a goodly number gathered together at the place of Mormon, to hear the words of Alma. Yea, all were gathered together that believed on his word, to hear him. And he did teach them, and did preach unto them repentance, and redemption, and faith on the Lord.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s people flee to Helam
routes.text: Alma’s people fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

mosiah-19.summary: Gideon, a strong man who opposes Noah, attacks the king as a Lamanite army arrives. Noah flees, leaving many families behind. His people later kill him by fire. Noah's son Limhi becomes king under a tribute agreement.

verse.text: Therefore the Lamanites did spare their lives, and took them captives and carried them back to the land of Nephi, and granted unto them that they might possess the land, under the conditions that they would deliver up king Noah into the hands of the Lamanites, and deliver up their property, even one half of all they possessed, one half of their gold, and their silver, and all their precious things, and thus they should pay tribute to the king of the Lamanites from year to year.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-20.summary: Noah's former priests take Lamanite daughters from Shemlon, a nearby Lamanite land. The Lamanites blame Limhi's people and attack. Limhi learns the cause and spares their wounded king. The king returns with them and restores peace.

verse.text: And now the priests of king Noah, being ashamed to return to the city of Nephi, yea, and also fearing that the people would slay them, therefore they durst not return to their wives and their children.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-21.summary: Limhi's people suffer under Lamanite control. Repeated attempts to fight free fail. They humble themselves and receive some relief. Ammon's arrival from Zarahemla gives them hope of escape.

verse.text: But when he found that they were not, but that they were his brethren, and had come from the land of Zarahemla, he was filled with exceedingly great joy.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Limhi’s explorers miss Zarahemla
routes.text: Forty-three men looked for Zarahemla. They found a land of bones and returned.

mosiah-22.summary: Limhi and Ammon seek a way out of bondage. Gideon proposes getting the guards drunk. The people leave with their families, flocks, and records. They reach Zarahemla while their pursuers become lost.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the people of king Limhi did depart by night into the wilderness with their flocks and their herds, and they went round about the land of Shilom in the wilderness, and bent their course towards the land of Zarahemla, being led by Ammon and his brethren.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Limhi’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: Limhi’s people went around the land of Shilom toward Zarahemla.

routes.title: A Lamanite army gets lost
routes.text: The army lost the trail. It found Amulon and then Helam.

mosiah-23.summary: Alma and his believers flee from Noah's army. They settle in a land they call Helam. Alma refuses to become their king. A lost Lamanite army finds them and Noah's former priests. Amulon, the leader of those priests, gains authority over Alma's people.

verse.text: And Amulon and his brethren did join the Lamanites, and they were traveling in the wilderness in search of the land of Nephi when they discovered the land of Helam, which was possessed by Alma and his brethren.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s people flee to Helam
routes.text: Alma’s people fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

routes.title: A Lamanite army gets lost
routes.text: The army lost the trail. It found Amulon and then Helam.

mosiah-24.summary: Amulon burdens Alma's people and forbids their prayers. They pray silently, and the Lord strengthens them. The Lord causes their guards to sleep. They escape through the wilderness and reach Zarahemla.

verse.text: And after they had been in the wilderness twelve days they arrived in the land of Zarahemla; and king Mosiah did also receive them with joy.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: One day to the valley of Alma, then twelve more days to Zarahemla.

mosiah-25.summary: Mosiah gathers the people and reads the records of the returning groups. The people grieve and rejoice at what they hear. Alma teaches and baptizes Limhi's people. Churches are organized throughout the land.

verse.text: Now there were not so many of the children of Nephi, or so many of those who were descendants of Nephi, as there were of the people of Zarahemla, who was a descendant of Mulek, and those who came with him into the wilderness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-26.summary: Some younger people reject the church's teachings. Alma brings their cases to Mosiah, who returns them. Alma prays and receives instructions from the Lord. He teaches repentance and removes those who refuse it.

verse.text: Blessed art thou, Alma, and blessed are they who were baptized in the waters of Mormon. Thou art blessed because of thy exceeding faith in the words alone of my servant Abinadi.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-27.summary: Alma's son, also named Alma, works against the church. Four sons of King Mosiah join him. An angel stops them and calls the younger Alma to repent. He recovers after the people pray and describes his change. The men begin to repair the harm they caused.

verse.text: And they traveled throughout all the land of Zarahemla, and among all the people who were under the reign of king Mosiah, zealously striving to repair all the injuries which they had done to the church, confessing all their sins, and publishing all the things which they had seen, and explaining the prophecies and the scriptures to all who desired to hear them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-28.summary: Mosiah's sons, Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, ask to teach the Lamanites. The Lord tells Mosiah to let them go. Mosiah translates the records found by Limhi's people. He gives the younger Alma charge of the sacred records.

verse.text: Now it came to pass that after the sons of Mosiah had done all these things, they took a small number with them and returned to their father, the king, and desired of him that he would grant unto them that they might, with these whom they had selected, go up to the land of Nephi that they might preach the things which they had heard, and that they might impart the word of God to their brethren, the Lamanites—
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mosiah-29.summary: Mosiah explains the dangers of rule by a wicked king. He proposes judges chosen by the people. The people accept, and the younger Alma becomes chief judge. Mosiah and the elder Alma die.

verse.text: And thus commenced the reign of the judges throughout all the land of Zarahemla, among all the people who were called the Nephites; and Alma was the first and chief judge.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-1.summary: Nehor, a man who preaches for money, kills Gideon. Gideon is an old man who once helped free Limhi's people. Alma, the chief judge, judges Nehor under the law. Persecution continues after Nehor's death. Church members share their goods and care for the poor.

verse.text: And it came to pass that they took him; and his name was Nehor; and they carried him upon the top of the hill Manti, and there he was caused, or rather did acknowledge, between the heavens and the earth, that what he had taught to the people was contrary to the word of God; and there he suffered an ignominious death.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-2.summary: Amlici, a follower of Nehor's ideas, wants to become king. The people reject him. His followers rebel and join a Lamanite army. Alma leads the Nephites in battles near Zarahemla and the river Sidon. The enemy retreats into Hermounts, a wilderness of wild beasts.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the Amlicites came upon the hill Amnihu, which was east of the river Sidon, which ran by the land of Zarahemla, and there they began to make war with the Nephites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The Amlicite battles
routes.text: The fight moved from Amnihu to Gideon, then back to the river crossing.

alma-3.summary: The Nephites bury their dead after the battles. The record describes the Amlicites' identifying marks. Another Lamanite attack follows. The chapter closes by linking each person's choices to their reward.

verse.text: Now it came to pass that not many days after the battle which was fought in the land of Zarahemla, by the Lamanites and the Amlicites, that there was another army of the Lamanites came in upon the people of Nephi, in the same place where the first army met the Amlicites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-4.summary: War leads many people to humble themselves. Later wealth brings pride and neglect of the poor. Alma sees that the church needs correction. He gives the judgment seat to Nephihah, a wise church elder. Alma then leaves to preach.

verse.text: Now it came to pass in the sixth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi, there were no contentions nor wars in the land of Zarahemla;
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-5.summary: Alma reminds Zarahemla's people of their fathers' deliverance. He asks whether their hearts have changed. He warns against pride, envy, and mistreatment of others. He calls both church members and others to repentance.

verse.text: Now it came to pass that Alma began to deliver the word of God unto the people, first in the land of Zarahemla, and from thence throughout all the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-6.summary: Alma puts the church in Zarahemla in order. Those who repent receive baptism. The people meet, fast, and pray for those outside the church. Alma crosses the river Sidon to teach in the land of Gideon.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that after Alma had made an end of speaking unto the people of the church, which was established in the city of Zarahemla, he ordained priests and elders, by laying on his hands according to the order of God, to preside and watch over the church.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma goes over to Gideon
routes.text: Alma went over to the east of the river Sidon, into the valley of Gideon.

alma-7.summary: Alma speaks to the people in Gideon. He foretells Christ's birth and suffering for his people. He asks them to repent and receive baptism. He urges faith, hope, charity, and care for God's commandments.

verse.text: And behold, I have come having great hopes and much desire that I should find that ye had humbled yourselves before God, and that ye had continued in the supplicating of his grace, that I should find that ye were blameless before him, that I should find that ye were not in the awful dilemma that our brethren were in at Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma goes over to Gideon
routes.text: Alma went over to the east of the river Sidon, into the valley of Gideon.

alma-8.summary: Alma teaches in the land of Melek. He then goes north to the city of Ammonihah. The people reject him. An angel sends him back, and Amulek, a man of Ammonihah, welcomes him. The two men prepare to preach together.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that Alma returned from the land of Gideon, after having taught the people of Gideon many things which cannot be written, having established the order of the church, according as he had before done in the land of Zarahemla, yea, he returned to his own house at Zarahemla to rest himself from the labors which he had performed.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
routes.text: Alma went to Melek, then three days north to Ammonihah, then Sidom.

alma-9.summary: The people challenge Alma's authority and words. He recalls the Lord's help to their ancestors. Their knowledge makes their rejection especially serious. He warns of destruction and the coming Son of God.

verse.text: And again, I, Alma, having been commanded of God that I should take Amulek and go forth and preach again unto this people, or the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, it came to pass as I began to preach unto them, they began to contend with me, saying:
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-10.summary: Amulek tells how an angel led him to welcome Alma. He confirms Alma's words. Lawyers try to trap him through questions. He warns that the prayers of the righteous preserve the city.

verse.text: Now these are the words which Amulek preached unto the people who were in the land of Ammonihah, saying:
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-14.summary: The people cast out believing men and burn women, children, and scriptures. Alma and Amulek witness the deaths and suffer in prison. They pray for strength. The prison falls, and they escape.

verse.text: And it came to pass after they had thus suffered for many days, (and it was on the twelfth day, in the tenth month, in the tenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi) that the chief judge over the land of Ammonihah and many of their teachers and their lawyers went in unto the prison where Alma and Amulek were bound with cords.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-15.summary: Alma and Amulek find refugees in the land of Sidom. Zeezrom asks for healing and expresses faith in Christ. Alma heals him, and he receives baptism. Alma establishes the church and later takes Amulek home.

verse.text: Now as I said, Alma having seen all these things, therefore he took Amulek and came over to the land of Zarahemla, and took him to his own house, and did administer unto him in his tribulations, and strengthened him in the Lord.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
routes.text: Alma went to Melek, then three days north to Ammonihah, then Sidom.

alma-16.summary: Lamanites destroy Ammonihah and take captives from nearby lands. Alma tells Zoram, the Nephite chief captain, where to find the enemy. The army recovers the captives near the Sidon. Alma and Amulek continue to teach throughout the land.

verse.text: And it came to pass in the eleventh year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi, on the fifth day of the second month, there having been much peace in the land of Zarahemla, there having been no wars nor contentions for a certain number of years, even until the fifth day of the second month in the eleventh year, there was a cry of war heard throughout the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

alma-17.summary: Alma meets Mosiah's sons after their mission. The account returns to their journey among the Lamanites. Ammon, one of Mosiah's sons, goes to the land of Ishmael. He becomes a servant of Lamoni, the Lamanite king there. He protects the king's flocks from attackers.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that as Alma was journeying from the land of Gideon southward, away to the land of Manti, behold, to his astonishment, he met with the sons of Mosiah journeying towards the land of Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons of Mosiah go up to Nephi
routes.text: They journeyed many days in the wilderness to reach the land of Nephi.

alma-18.summary: Lamoni hears what Ammon did for his servants. He wonders whether Ammon is the Great Spirit. Ammon teaches him about God, creation, and redemption. Lamoni prays for mercy and falls to the earth.

verse.text: And they said unto him: Behold, he is feeding thy horses. Now the king had commanded his servants, previous to the time of the watering of their flocks, that they should prepare his horses and chariots, and conduct him forth to the land of Nephi; for there had been a great feast appointed at the land of Nephi, by the father of Lamoni, who was king over all the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-20.summary: Ammon and Lamoni travel toward Middoni to free Ammon's brother Aaron and his companions. They meet Lamoni's father, the king over all the Lamanite lands. He commands his son to kill Ammon. Ammon resists the king and spares his life. The king permits his son's freedom and the prisoners' release.

verse.text: And it came to pass that when they had established a church in that land, that king Lamoni desired that Ammon should go with him to the land of Nephi, that he might show him unto his father.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-21.summary: Aaron, Ammon's brother, teaches in a Lamanite city called Jerusalem. He then teaches in the village of Ani-Anti. Many reject his words. He and his companions suffer in prison in Middoni. After their release, they continue teaching while Ammon serves Lamoni's people.

verse.text: Now when Ammon and his brethren separated themselves in the borders of the land of the Lamanites, behold Aaron took his journey towards the land which was called by the Lamanites, Jerusalem, calling it after the land of their fathers' nativity; and it was away joining the borders of Mormon.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-22.summary: Aaron teaches Lamoni's father about God and redemption. The king prays and falls to the earth. Aaron raises him, and the household believes. Mormon, the editor of the record, then describes the lands. He names the seas, the wilderness, and the narrow neck.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the king sent a proclamation throughout all the land, amongst all his people who were in all his land, who were in all the regions round about, which was bordering even to the sea, on the east and on the west, and which was divided from the land of Zarahemla by a narrow strip of wilderness, which ran from the sea east even to the sea west, and round about on the borders of the seashore, and the borders of the wilderness which was on the north by the land of Zarahemla, through the borders of Manti, by the head of the river Sidon, running from the east towards the west—and thus were the Lamanites and the Nephites divided.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla go up the Sidon
routes.text: They came from the place of landing up into the south wilderness.

alma-23.summary: The king protects the missionaries throughout his lands. Many Lamanites believe and give up rebellion. The record names communities that accept the teaching. The converts take the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies.

verse.text: And also of the people of the Lamanites who were in the city of Nephi;
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-24.summary: Enemies prepare to attack the converted Lamanites. Their new king, Lamoni's brother, asks them to keep their promise against killing. They bury their weapons and refuse to fight. Many attackers repent after killing people who offer no resistance.

verse.text: And it came to pass that their brethren, the Lamanites, made preparations for war, and came up to the land of Nephi for the purpose of destroying the king, and to place another in his stead, and also of destroying the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi out of the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-25.summary: Lamanite armies attack the Nephites and destroy Ammonihah. Some descendants of Noah's priests suffer death. Many Lamanites later join the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Mosiah's sons rejoice in the mission's results.

verse.text: But they took their armies and went over into the borders of the land of Zarahemla, and fell upon the people who were in the land of Ammonihah and destroyed them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

alma-26.summary: Ammon recalls the missionaries' hardships and the many converts. Aaron warns him against boasting. Ammon gives the credit to God's strength and mercy. He rejoices that God remembers every people.

verse.text: And now, these are the words of Ammon to his brethren, which say thus: My brothers and my brethren, behold I say unto you, how great reason have we to rejoice; for could we have supposed when we started from the land of Zarahemla that God would have granted unto us such great blessings?
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-27.summary: Renewed attacks threaten the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Ammon asks the Lord whether they should leave. The Nephites give them Jershon and provide protection. They become known as the people of Ammon.

verse.text: Let us gather together this people of the Lord, and let us go down to the land of Zarahemla to our brethren the Nephites, and flee out of the hands of our enemies, that we be not destroyed.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Jershon
routes.text: The converted Lamanites left Nephi. The Nephites gave them the land of Jershon.

alma-28.summary: A great battle follows the settlement in Jershon. Many families mourn their dead. Some grieve without hope, while others trust God's promises. The record recalls the missionaries' work and its results.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that after the people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon, and a church also established in the land of Jershon, and the armies of the Nephites were set round about the land of Jershon, yea, in all the borders round about the land of Zarahemla; behold the armies of the Lamanites had followed their brethren into the wilderness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-29.summary: Alma wishes he could speak with an angel's power. He then accepts the work God has given him. He rejoices in the repentance of others. He also celebrates his companions' success among the Lamanites.

verse.text: But I do not joy in my own success alone, but my joy is more full because of the success of my brethren, who have been up to the land of Nephi.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-30.summary: Korihor, a man who preaches against Christ, comes to Zarahemla. He teaches that no Christ will come. The people of Gideon bind him. Their leaders send him to Alma, the high priest in Zarahemla. Korihor demands a sign and loses his ability to speak. He confesses his deception. He later dies among the Zoramites, a group of Nephite dissenters.

verse.text: But it came to pass in the latter end of the seventeenth year, there came a man into the land of Zarahemla, and he was Anti-Christ, for he began to preach unto the people against the prophecies which had been spoken by the prophets, concerning the coming of Christ.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-31.summary: The Zoramites, Nephite dissenters led by a man named Zoram, live in Antionum. Alma leads companions there to teach them. They see the Zoramites repeat a prayer from a high stand. The prayer rejects Christ and claims special favor. Alma prays for strength and for the people's return.

verse.text: Now the Zoramites had gathered themselves together in a land which they called Antionum, which was east of the land of Zarahemla, which lay nearly bordering upon the seashore, which was south of the land of Jershon, which also bordered upon the wilderness south, which wilderness was full of the Lamanites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-35.summary: The Zoramites expel those who believe the missionaries. The people of Ammon welcome them in Jershon. Threats follow, and the people of Ammon move to Melek. Alma gathers his sons to give each one counsel.

verse.text: And Alma, and Ammon, and their brethren, and also the two sons of Alma returned to the land of Zarahemla, after having been instruments in the hands of God of bringing many of the Zoramites to repentance; and as many as were brought to repentance were driven out of their land; but they have lands for their inheritance in the land of Jershon, and they have taken up arms to defend themselves, and their wives, and children, and their lands.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Melek
routes.text: The people of Ammon left Jershon and came over into the land of Melek.

alma-39.summary: Alma rebukes his son Corianton for abandoning his mission. Corianton went after Isabel, a harlot among the Zoramites. His conduct has harmed the Zoramites' response to the teaching. Alma tells him to repent and repair his wrongs. He explains why they proclaim Christ before his coming.

verse.text: And this is not all, my son. Thou didst do that which was grievous unto me; for thou didst forsake the ministry, and did go over into the land of Siron among the borders of the Lamanites, after the harlot Isabel.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-43.summary: Zerahemnah, a Lamanite commander, leads an army against the Nephites. Moroni, the young chief captain of the Nephites, prepares defenses. These defenses cause the enemy to leave Antionum for Manti. Moroni places troops on both sides of the Sidon. The Nephites surround the enemy, and Moroni stops the killing.

verse.text: Behold, now it came to pass that they durst not come against the Nephites in the borders of Jershon; therefore they departed out of the land of Antionum into the wilderness, and took their journey round about in the wilderness, away by the head of the river Sidon, that they might come into the land of Manti and take possession of the land; for they did not suppose that the armies of Moroni would know whither they had gone.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites go “round about” to Manti
routes.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and went round about by the head of Sidon.

routes.title: Moroni marches to Manti
routes.text: Moroni left part of his army in Jershon and marched to the land of Manti.

alma-45.summary: Alma asks Helaman about his faith. He foretells the future destruction of the Nephites. Alma leaves and is not seen again. Helaman and his companions organize churches as pride spreads.

verse.text: And when Alma had done this he departed out of the land of Zarahemla, as if to go into the land of Melek. And it came to pass that he was never heard of more; as to his death or burial we know not of.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-46.summary: Amalickiah, a Nephite dissenter, seeks to become king with support from other dissenters. Captain Moroni raises a written pledge of freedom and faith. The people covenant to defend those commitments. Amalickiah escapes while many of his followers return.

verse.text: And it came to pass that Amalickiah fled with a small number of his men, and the remainder were delivered up into the hands of Moroni and were taken back into the land of Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-47.summary: Amalickiah uses deception to control a Lamanite army. He arranges the death of Lehonti, a Lamanite leader. His servants kill the Lamanite king and blame others. Amalickiah marries the queen and becomes king.

verse.text: Now when the servants of the king saw an army pursuing after them, they were frightened again, and fled into the wilderness, and came over into the land of Zarahemla and joined the people of Ammon.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-48.summary: Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites against the Nephites. Moroni strengthens cities and places defenses at weak points. Mormon describes Moroni's faith and care for freedom. The Nephites prepare for war despite their desire for peace.

verse.text: And it came to pass that they took their camp, and moved forth toward the land of Zarahemla in the wilderness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-49.summary: Lamanite armies find Ammonihah strongly defended. They turn to the city of Noah and find defenses there too. Their attack fails with heavy losses. The Nephites give thanks and enjoy peace.

verse.text: And now it came to pass in the eleventh month of the nineteenth year, on the tenth day of the month, the armies of the Lamanites were seen approaching towards the land of Ammonihah.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

alma-50.summary: Moroni strengthens the frontier and establishes eastern cities. The people of two cities, Lehi and Morianton, dispute land. Morianton, their leader, takes his people toward the land northward. Teancum, a Nephite commander, stops them at the narrow pass. Pahoran, the son of Nephihah, later becomes chief judge.

verse.text: And it came to pass that Moroni caused that his armies should go forth into the east wilderness; yea, and they went forth and drove all the Lamanites who were in the east wilderness into their own lands, which were south of the land of Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Morianton flees toward the land northward
routes.text: Morianton’s people fled toward the land northward. They were stopped by the narrow pass.

routes.title: Teancum heads off Morianton
routes.text: Moroni sent an army to head off Morianton. They met him at the pass.

alma-51.summary: The king-men, who want a king, divide the Nephites. Moroni suppresses them as Amalickiah attacks eastern cities. The army reaches the borders near Bountiful. Teancum enters its camp and kills Amalickiah.

verse.text: Now his armies were not so great as they had hitherto been, because of the many thousands who had been slain by the hand of the Nephites; but notwithstanding their great loss, Amalickiah had gathered together a wonderfully great army, insomuch that he feared not to come down to the land of Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
routes.text: Amalickiah took city after city on the east borders by the seashore.

alma-52.summary: Ammoron, Amalickiah's brother, becomes the Lamanite king and continues the war. Moroni and Teancum plan to draw troops out of the city of Mulek. Teancum retreats toward Bountiful while other troops take the city. The pursuing Lamanites are surrounded and captured.

verse.text: Now, the king (Ammoron) had departed out of the land of Zarahemla, and had made known unto the queen concerning the death of his brother, and had gathered together a large number of men, and had marched forth against the Nephites on the borders by the west sea.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Teancum draws the Lamanites out of Mulek
routes.text: The Lamanites chased Teancum down by the seashore until they came near Bountiful.

alma-53.summary: Prisoners work on defenses near Bountiful. Trouble continues on the western front. The people of Ammon consider breaking their promise against fighting. Two thousand of their sons enlist instead. Helaman, Alma's son, becomes their leader.

verse.text: And now behold, I have somewhat to say concerning the people of Ammon, who, in the beginning, were Lamanites; but by Ammon and his brethren, or rather by the power and word of God, they had been converted unto the Lord; and they had been brought down into the land of Zarahemla, and had ever since been protected by the Nephites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-54.summary: Ammoron proposes an exchange of prisoners. Moroni asks for Nephite families as well as soldiers. He demands that the invaders leave the land. Ammoron accepts the exchange terms but rejects Moroni's demands for peace.

verse.text: Behold, I would tell you somewhat concerning the justice of God, and the sword of his almighty wrath, which doth hang over you except ye repent and withdraw your armies into your own lands, or the land of your possessions, which is the land of Nephi.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-55.summary: Moroni refuses to proceed with the exchange. He sends wine to the guards at the city of Gid through a Lamanite servant. The prisoners receive weapons while the guards sleep. The Nephites take the city without killing the guards.

verse.text: And it came to pass that when he had fortified the city Gid, according to his desires, he caused that his prisoners should be taken to the city Bountiful; and he also guarded that city with an exceedingly strong force.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-56.summary: Helaman writes to Moroni about the western war. His young soldiers join Antipus, a Nephite commander, at the city of Judea. They draw the enemy away from Antiparah. They fight after Antipus falls, and all Helaman's young men survive.

verse.text: Neither durst they march down against the city of Zarahemla; neither durst they cross the head of Sidon, over to the city of Nephihah.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Helaman’s young men march to Judea
routes.text: Helaman marched the two thousand young men to the city of Judea.

routes.title: Helaman lures the army out of Antiparah
routes.text: They marched near Antiparah as if going to the city by the seashore.

alma-57.summary: Helaman's army receives reinforcements and takes Cumeni. A large group of prisoners attempts to escape. Lamanites attack the Nephites while part of the army is away. Helaman's young soldiers hold firm, and none of them dies.

verse.text: And it came to pass that in the commencement of the twenty and ninth year, we received a supply of provisions, and also an addition to our army, from the land of Zarahemla, and from the land round about, to the number of six thousand men, besides sixty of the sons of the Ammonites who had come to join their brethren, my little band of two thousand. And now behold, we were strong, yea, and we had also plenty of provisions brought unto us.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-58.summary: Helaman's army waits for supplies and men. They pray for strength and receive assurance. Gid and Teomner, two of Helaman's officers, hide near Manti. They take the city while Helaman draws its army away. Helaman ends his letter with concern about limited government support.

verse.text: Yea, and it became expedient that we should employ our men to the maintaining those parts of the land which we had regained of our possessions; therefore it became expedient that we should wait, that we might receive more strength from the land of Zarahemla and also a new supply of provisions.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-59.summary: Moroni rejoices at Helaman's letter and asks for help. A growing Lamanite force attacks Nephihah. The city falls, and survivors flee to Moroni. He fears that the government has failed his armies.

verse.text: And it came to pass when Moroni had sent this epistle to the land of Zarahemla, he began again to lay a plan that he might obtain the remainder of those possessions and cities which the Lamanites had taken from them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-60.summary: Moroni writes to Pahoran, the chief judge. He accuses Pahoran and the government of neglecting the armies. He recalls the soldiers who have died without help. He demands supplies and troops. He threatens action if the government continues to refuse.

verse.text: And it came to pass that he wrote again to the governor of the land, who was Pahoran, and these are the words which he wrote, saying: Behold, I direct mine epistle to Pahoran, in the city of Zarahemla, who is the chief judge and the governor over the land, and also to all those who have been chosen by this people to govern and manage the affairs of this war.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-61.summary: Pahoran tells Moroni that king-men have driven him from Zarahemla. He is gathering supporters in Gideon. He accepts Moroni's concern without anger. He asks Moroni to come and help restore the government.

verse.text: They have got possession of the land, or the city, of Zarahemla; they have appointed a king over them, and he hath written unto the king of the Lamanites, in the which he hath joined an alliance with him; in the which alliance he hath agreed to maintain the city of Zarahemla, which maintenance he supposeth will enable the Lamanites to conquer the remainder of the land, and he shall be placed king over this people when they shall be conquered under the Lamanites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-62.summary: Moroni joins Pahoran and defeats the rebels in Zarahemla. The Nephites retake Nephihah and other eastern cities. Teancum kills Ammoron but dies during the attempt. Peace returns, and Helaman teaches until his death.

verse.text: And thus, when Moroni had gathered together whatsoever men he could in all his march, he came to the land of Gideon; and uniting his forces with those of Pahoran they became exceedingly strong, even stronger than the men of Pachus, who was the king of those dissenters who had driven the freemen out of the land of Zarahemla and had taken possession of the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Moroni retakes the east coast
routes.text: The Lamanites fled from city to city, then down to the seashore and Moroni.

alma-63.summary: Shiblon, Helaman's brother, receives the records after Helaman's death. Many people move to the land northward. Hagoth, a ship builder, builds ships by the west sea. Shiblon later gives the records to Helaman's son, also named Helaman.

verse.text: And it came to pass that in the thirty and seventh year of the reign of the judges, there was a large company of men, even to the amount of five thousand and four hundred men, with their wives and their children, departed out of the land of Zarahemla into the land which was northward.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Hagoth’s ships sail north
routes.text: Hagoth launched ships into the west sea. Some went to the land northward.

routes.title: Nephites spread into the land northward
routes.text: Many people went forth unto the land northward and spread out.

helaman-1.summary: Three sons of Pahoran, the late chief judge, compete for the judgment seat. Kishkumen, a hired murderer, kills Pahoran's son, the chosen ruler. Coriantumr, a Nephite dissenter, leads a Lamanite army into Zarahemla. Moronihah, Captain Moroni's son, and Lehi, another captain, surround the invaders. They retake the city.

verse.text: And they came down again that they might pitch battle against the Nephites. And they were led by a man whose name was Coriantumr; and he was a descendant of Zarahemla; and he was a dissenter from among the Nephites; and he was a large and a mighty man.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Coriantumr strikes the center
routes.text: A Lamanite army came into the center of the land and took Zarahemla.

helaman-3.summary: Many people settle in the land northward. The record describes their building materials and records. The church gains many members during years of peace. Pride returns, and Helaman's son Nephi later becomes chief judge.

verse.text: And it came to pass in the forty and sixth, yea, there was much contention and many dissensions; in the which there were an exceedingly great many who departed out of the land of Zarahemla, and went forth unto the land northward to inherit the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Hagoth’s ships sail north
routes.text: Hagoth launched ships into the west sea. Some went to the land northward.

routes.title: Nephites spread into the land northward
routes.text: Many people went forth unto the land northward and spread out.

helaman-4.summary: Dissenters join the Lamanites in renewed war. The Nephites retreat to Bountiful and fortify a line. Moronihah recovers some land as prophets call the people to repent. The people recognize that their own sins have weakened them.

verse.text: And in the fifty and seventh year they did come down against the Nephites to battle, and they did commence the work of death; yea, insomuch that in the fifty and eighth year of the reign of the judges they succeeded in obtaining possession of the land of Zarahemla; yea, and also all the lands, even unto the land which was near the land Bountiful.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Nephites driven into Bountiful
routes.text: The Nephites were driven into the land of Bountiful and fortified a line.

helaman-5.summary: Nephi leaves the judgment seat to preach with his brother Lehi. They travel from Bountiful through Gid, Mulek, Zarahemla, and Nephi. God's power protects them in prison. Many Lamanites believe and return occupied lands.

verse.text: And even from one city to another, until they had gone forth among all the people of Nephi who were in the land southward; and from thence into the land of Zarahemla, among the Lamanites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Nephi and Lehi preach from Bountiful
routes.text: They began at Bountiful, then Gid and Mulek, then Zarahemla and Nephi.

helaman-6.summary: Lamanites and Nephites trade and travel in peace. Many Lamanites teach the Nephites. Murders and secret agreements then spread among the Nephites. The Lamanites oppose the robbers while Nephite leaders support them.

verse.text: And it came to pass that many of the Lamanites did come down into the land of Zarahemla, and did declare unto the people of the Nephites the manner of their conversion, and did exhort them to faith and repentance.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla cross the sea
routes.text: The Lord brought Mulek’s people across the great waters into the land north.

helaman-7.summary: Nephi returns and finds corrupt leaders in power. He prays on his garden tower. A crowd gathers, and he calls them to repentance. He warns that rejection of God will bring destruction.

verse.text: Behold, now it came to pass in the sixty and ninth year of the reign of the judges over the people of the Nephites, that Nephi, the son of Helaman, returned to the land of Zarahemla from the land northward.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

helaman-13.summary: Samuel, a Lamanite prophet, comes to preach in Zarahemla. The Nephites cast him out. He returns and speaks from the city wall. He warns of destruction unless the people repent. He condemns their love of riches and rejection of prophets. He asks them to seek mercy before it is too late.

verse.text: And it came to pass that in this year there was one Samuel, a Lamanite, came into the land of Zarahemla, and began to preach unto the people. And it came to pass that he did preach, many days, repentance unto the people, and they did cast him out, and he was about to return to his own land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-1.summary: Unbelievers threaten those waiting for Samuel's promised sign. Nephi, the son of the earlier Nephi, prays for his people. The Lord promises that the sign will come. A night without darkness confirms Christ's birth. Belief spreads, but later dissent weakens some families.

verse.text: And Nephi, the son of Helaman, had departed out of the land of Zarahemla, giving charge unto his son Nephi, who was his eldest son, concerning the plates of brass, and all the records which had been kept, and all those things which had been kept sacred from the departure of Lehi out of Jerusalem.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-2.summary: The people begin to forget the signs. They count their years from Christ's birth. Robber bands threaten both Nephites and Lamanites. The two peoples join in defense, but divisions continue.

verse.text: And Nephi, who was the father of Nephi, who had the charge of the records, did not return to the land of Zarahemla, and could nowhere be found in all the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-3.summary: Giddianhi, the robbers' leader, demands that Lachoneus surrender. Lachoneus, the Nephite governor, refuses and gathers his people with supplies and flocks. Gidgiddoni, the chief captain, prepares defenses between Zarahemla and Bountiful. The people repent and prepare to withstand an attack.

verse.text: And the land which was appointed was the land of Zarahemla, and the land which was between the land Zarahemla and the land Bountiful, yea, to the line which was between the land Bountiful and the land Desolation.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: People gather from the south
routes.text: The people came from all parts of the land into one place.

routes.title: People gather from the north
routes.text: People in the land northward also came to the gathering place.

3-nephi-4.summary: The robbers find the abandoned lands without food. Giddianhi attacks the gathered people and dies. Zemnarihah, the next robber leader, tries a siege and later retreats. The defenders capture him and give thanks for their deliverance.

verse.text: And the robbers could not exist save it were in the wilderness, for the want of food; for the Nephites had left their lands desolate, and had gathered their flocks and their herds and all their substance, and they were in one body.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-5.summary: The people repent after the robbers' defeat. Prisoners receive a chance to leave their former ways. Mormon explains his work in preserving the records. He looks toward Israel's gathering through Jesus Christ.

verse.text: And behold, I am called Mormon, being called after the land of Mormon, the land in which Alma did establish the church among the people, yea, the first church which was established among them after their transgression.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-6.summary: The people return to their lands and rebuild. Wealth and rank divide them. Some judges secretly kill people who testify of Christ. Their allies plot to destroy the governor and establish a king.

verse.text: Therefore a complaint came up unto the land of Zarahemla, to the governor of the land, against these judges who had condemned the prophets of the Lord unto death, not according to the law.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-8.summary: The people await the sign of Christ's death. A great storm destroys cities, roads, and land. Zarahemla burns, and the city of Moroni sinks into the sea. Earth covers the city of Moronihah. Darkness follows, and survivors mourn their refusal to repent.

verse.text: And the city of Zarahemla did take fire.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-9.summary: A voice names cities destroyed for their wickedness. The speaker identifies himself as Jesus Christ. He invites the survivors to come to him and receive healing. He asks for a broken heart and a repentant spirit.

verse.text: Behold, that great city Zarahemla have I burned with fire, and the inhabitants thereof.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

3-nephi-11.summary: People gather near the temple in Bountiful. The Father introduces his Son, and Jesus descends. The people touch his wounds and witness his resurrection. He calls disciples and teaches baptism without dispute.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that there were a great multitude gathered together, of the people of Nephi, round about the temple which was in the land Bountiful; and they were marveling and wondering one with another, and were showing one to another the great and marvelous change which had taken place.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

4-nephi-1.summary: The people live together in faith after Christ's visit. They share their goods and have no disputes. Later pride, separate churches, and old divisions return. Ammaron, a record keeper, hides the sacred records as wickedness spreads.

verse.text: Yea, even that great city Zarahemla did they cause to be built again.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mormon-1.summary: Ammaron tells Mormon, a boy of about ten, where to find the records. Mormon travels with his father to Zarahemla. War begins near the Sidon. Mormon knows the Lord but cannot teach a people who reject repentance.

verse.text: And it came to pass that I, being eleven years old, was carried by my father into the land southward, even to the land of Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mormon-2.summary: Mormon becomes commander while still young. His army loses cities and retreats through Joshua, Jashon, and Shem. Their sorrow does not lead to true repentance. A treaty gives the Nephites the land northward.

verse.text: And we marched forth and came to the land of Joshua, which was in the borders west by the seashore.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Mormon’s army leaves the land southward
routes.text: The Nephites lost Angola and David. They moved to Joshua, then fled north.

mormon-3.summary: Mormon strengthens defenses at Desolation and the narrow pass. The Nephites repel attacks but boast and vow revenge. Mormon refuses to lead them in that purpose. He turns to warning the future readers of his record.

verse.text: And it came to pass that I did cause my people that they should gather themselves together at the land Desolation, to a city which was in the borders, by the narrow pass which led into the land southward.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites cross the neck
routes.text: The Lamanites came down to the city of Desolation to battle.

mormon-4.summary: The Nephites attack the Lamanites and are driven back. Desolation and Teancum change hands in repeated battles. Cruelty increases as the Nephites retreat to Boaz. Mormon retrieves the records from the hill Shim before the land falls.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that in the three hundred and sixty and third year the Nephites did go up with their armies to battle against the Lamanites, out of the land Desolation.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.

routes.title: Lamanites cross the neck
routes.text: The Lamanites came down to the city of Desolation to battle.

mormon-5.summary: Mormon agrees to lead the Nephites again. They hold Jordan for a time, then flee. Mormon describes the record's future purpose for their descendants. He also calls the Gentiles to repentance.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the Lamanites did come against us as we had fled to the city of Jordan; but behold, they were driven back that they did not take the city at that time.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.

mormon-6.summary: Mormon gathers his people in the land of Cumorah. He hides most records in the hill Cumorah. He gives some plates to his son Moroni. A great battle destroys the Nephite armies. Mormon mourns the people who would not repent.

verse.text: And I, Mormon, wrote an epistle unto the king of the Lamanites, and desired of him that he would grant unto us that we might gather together our people unto the land of Cumorah, by a hill which was called Cumorah, and there we could give them battle.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.

mormon-8.summary: Moroni, Mormon's son, describes his father's death and his own isolation. He writes about the record's future appearance. He warns those who oppose God's work. He also condemns future readers' pride and neglect of the poor.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that after the great and tremendous battle at Cumorah, behold, the Nephites who had escaped into the country southward were hunted by the Lamanites, until they were all destroyed.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

ether-1.summary: Moroni, Mormon's son, begins a short form of the Jaredite record. The Jaredites are an earlier people from the time of the great tower. Moroni first traces the family line of Ether, their last prophet. Jared asks his brother to pray during the confusion of languages. The Lord preserves their language. He promises to lead their families to a chosen land.

verse.text: Coriantor was the son of Moron.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

ether-1.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.

ether-7.summary: Orihah's descendants fight for power. Corihor rebels against his father, King Kib, and takes him captive. Kib's son Shule restores him. Later rebellions divide the kingdom again. Shule protects prophets and calls the people to repentance.

verse.text: Now the land of Moron, where the king dwelt, was near the land which is called Desolation by the Nephites.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

ether-7.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.

ether-9.summary: The Lord warns Omer, who leaves for a place called Ablom. Akish's rule collapses through family conflict and war. Later kings bring prosperity. Then Heth, a king's son, turns against the prophets. Famine ends after the people humble themselves.

verse.text: And there came forth poisonous serpents also upon the face of the land, and did poison many people. And it came to pass that their flocks began to flee before the poisonous serpents, towards the land southward, which was called by the Nephites Zarahemla.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Omer flees from Moron
routes.text: Omer passed by the hill Shim and Cumorah to a place called Ablom.

ether-9.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.
