ether-10.summary: Shez, a son of Heth, rebuilds the people after famine. Later rulers vary in justice and oppression. The record describes farming, trade, tools, and work under King Lib. Secret robbers return despite King Com's efforts against them.

verse.text: And they built a great city by the narrow neck of land, by the place where the sea divides the land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

ether-10.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.

ether-11.summary: Prophets repeatedly warn the Jaredites to repent. Many rulers and people reject them. Wars, captivity, and political changes continue. The record's family line reaches Ether.

verse.text: And it came to pass that Ethem did execute judgment in wickedness all his days; and he begat Moron. And it came to pass that Moron did reign in his stead; and Moron did that which was wicked before the Lord.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

ether-11.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.

ether-14.summary: Coriantumr fights repeated battles against rival leaders. Shiz, the brother of a rival named Lib, takes command after Lib dies. Both armies leave cities and families destroyed. The struggle continues toward the eastern waters.

verse.text: And they pitched their tents in the valley of Corihor; and Coriantumr pitched his tents in the valley of Shurr. Now the valley of Shurr was near the hill Comnor; wherefore, Coriantumr did gather his armies together upon the hill Comnor, and did sound a trumpet unto the armies of Shiz to invite them forth to battle.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The last Jaredite war
routes.text: The war moved east to the hill Comnor, north to Ripliancum, then to Ramah.

ether-14.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.

ether-15.summary: Coriantumr remembers Ether's warning and seeks peace, but Shiz refuses. The armies move from the waters of Ripliancum toward Ogath and Ramah. They gather the remaining people for battle. Coriantumr kills Shiz after their armies are destroyed.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the army of Coriantumr did pitch their tents by the hill Ramah; and it was that same hill where my father Mormon did hide up the records unto the Lord, which were sacred.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The last Jaredite war
routes.text: The war moved east to the hill Comnor, north to Ripliancum, then to Ramah.

ether-15.dateDetail: The Church edition gives no dates for the Jaredite record.

lehi-warns-jerusalem.summary: Nephi, a son of Lehi, begins his record in Jerusalem. It is the first year of King Zedekiah. Lehi prays for his people and sees God in a vision. He reads a heavenly book about Jerusalem's destruction. He warns the people and speaks of a coming Messiah. The people mock him and seek to kill him.

verse.text: And when the Jews heard these things they were angry with him; yea, even as with the prophets of old, whom they had cast out, and stoned, and slain; and they also sought his life, that they might take it away. But behold, I, Nephi, will show unto you that the tender mercies of the Lord are over all those whom he hath chosen, because of their faith, to make them mighty even unto the power of deliverance.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Babylon makes Zedekiah king in Jerusalem.

lehi-leaves-jerusalem.summary: The Lord tells Lehi in a dream to leave Jerusalem. Lehi takes his family into the wilderness near the Red Sea. They camp in a valley he names Lemuel. Laman and Lemuel, Nephi's older brothers, complain. Nephi prays, and the Lord softens his heart. The Lord promises Nephi a land if he keeps the commandments.

verse.text: And inasmuch as ye shall keep my commandments, ye shall prosper, and shall be led to a land of promise; yea, even a land which I have prepared for you; yea, a land which is choice above all other lands.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lehi’s family leaves Jerusalem
routes.text: The Lord told Lehi to leave Jerusalem. The family camped three days past the Red Sea borders.
routes.note: The road down the Arabah valley is one common proposal. The text names no road.

lehi-leaves-jerusalem.relatedNote: Lehi leaves as Babylon takes control of Judah.

nephi-gets-the-brass-plates.summary: Lehi sends his sons back to Jerusalem for the brass plates. Laban keeps this record. Nephi says the Lord prepares a way for what he commands. Laban refuses them and takes their property. Laman and Lemuel beat their younger brothers, and an angel stops them. Nephi goes into the city at night and finds Laban drunk. The Spirit tells him to kill Laban, and he takes the plates. Laban's servant Zoram joins the family.

verse.text: And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons return for the brass plates
routes.text: Nephi and his brothers went up to Jerusalem for the plates. They came back with the plates and Zoram.

ishmaels-family-joins.summary: The Lord tells Lehi that his sons should take wives. The sons return to Jerusalem for the family of Ishmael. On the way back, Laman and Lemuel and some of Ishmael's family rebel. They tie Nephi up and leave him to die. Nephi prays, and the ropes come loose. Some of Ishmael's family plead for him. The families return to Lehi and give thanks.

verse.text: Yea, and how is it that ye have forgotten that the Lord is able to do all things according to his will, for the children of men, if it so be that they exercise faith in him? Wherefore, let us be faithful to him.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons bring Ishmael’s family
routes.text: The sons went up to Jerusalem again. Ishmael’s family came down with them to the valley.

why-nephi-keeps-two-records.summary: Nephi says he will not give his family's full line of ancestors. He wants to persuade readers to come to the God of Abraham and be saved. He keeps two sets of plates. One holds the history of kings and wars. The other is mostly for teaching and prophecy. He says the Lord has a wise purpose for both.

verse.text: For the fulness of mine intent is that I may persuade men to come unto the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, and be saved.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

lehis-dream.summary: Lehi dreams of a tree whose fruit makes people happy. He eats it and calls his family to come. Sariah, Sam, and Nephi eat, but Laman and Lemuel will not come. People hold to an iron rod along a path through a mist of darkness. People in a great building mock those who eat. Lehi then speaks of Jerusalem's fall and the coming Messiah. He compares Israel to an olive tree whose branches are broken off.

verse.text: And it came to pass that I beheld a tree, whose fruit was desirable to make one happy.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

nephis-vision.summary: Nephi wants to see what his father saw. The Spirit shows him the tree. An angel says it is the love of God. He sees Mary and the Son of God. He sees Christ's ministry and death. He sees his descendants' wars and Christ's visit to them. He sees people cross the sea to a new land with a book. He sees two churches and the power given to God's covenant people.

verse.text: And I answered him, saying: Yea, it is the love of God, which sheddeth itself abroad in the hearts of the children of men; wherefore, it is the most desirable above all things.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Gabriel tells Mary she will bear a son.

nephi-answers-his-brothers.summary: Nephi returns to find his brothers arguing about Lehi's words. He asks if they have asked the Lord. He explains the olive tree as Israel scattered and later gathered. They ask what the iron rod means. He says it is the word of God. The river is the filth that separates the wicked from God.

verse.text: And I said unto them that it was the word of God; and whoso would hearken unto the word of God, and would hold fast unto it, they would never perish; neither could the temptations and the fiery darts of the adversary overpower them unto blindness, to lead them away to destruction.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

the-liahona.summary: Lehi's sons marry Ishmael's daughters. One morning Lehi finds a brass ball outside his tent. Its spindles point the way into the wilderness. Nephi breaks his steel bow, and the family has no food. He makes a new bow and asks his father where to hunt. The ball works as they have faith. Ishmael dies at a place called Nahom.

verse.text: And it came to pass that as my father arose in the morning, and went forth to the tent door, to his great astonishment he beheld upon the ground a round ball of curious workmanship; and it was of fine brass. And within the ball were two spindles; and the one pointed the way whither we should go into the wilderness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: From the valley to Nahom
routes.text: The family traveled south-southeast near the Red Sea. Nephi’s bow broke on the way. Ishmael died at Nahom.
routes.note: Researchers follow the old incense road east of the coastal mountains. The text names only Shazer and Nahom.

nephi-builds-a-ship.summary: After eight years in the wilderness, the family reaches a coast they call Bountiful. The Lord tells Nephi to build a ship. His brothers mock him. Nephi reminds them how the Lord divided the Red Sea for Moses. They try to throw him into the sea. The Lord shocks them by his power when they touch Nephi. They help him build the ship.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the Lord spake unto me, saying: Thou shalt construct a ship, after the manner which I shall show thee, that I may carry thy people across these waters.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: The Red Sea is divided before Israel.

routes.title: Eastward to Bountiful
routes.text: From Nahom the family traveled nearly eastward. After eight years in the wilderness they reached the sea.
routes.note: This line runs along the south edge of the great Arabian desert. The stops are not known.

voyage-to-the-promised-land.summary: The family finishes the ship and sails. Laman and Lemuel make merry and tie Nephi up. The compass stops working, and a great storm drives them back. After four days they untie Nephi. He prays, and the storm stops. They reach the promised land and plant their seeds.

verse.text: And it came to pass that after we had sailed for the space of many days we did arrive at the promised land; and we went forth upon the land, and did pitch our tents; and we did call it the promised land.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lehi’s family reaches the promised land
routes.text: The ship crossed the sea and arrived at the promised land.

nephites-and-lamanites-separate.summary: After Lehi dies, Laman and Lemuel seek to kill Nephi. The Lord warns Nephi to flee with those who will go with him. They settle in a land they call Nephi. They build a temple like Solomon's, but less costly. They work the land and keep the law of Moses. Nephi says they live in happiness. The people who stay with Laman are called Lamanites.

verse.text: And it came to pass that we lived after the manner of happiness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Nephi’s people move to the land of Nephi
routes.text: Nephi’s people fled into the wilderness for many days. They called the new place Nephi.

the-people-of-zarahemla.summary: Five of Jacob's descendants keep the small plates in turn. Amaleki, the last, tells how the Lord warns Mosiah to leave the land of Nephi. Mosiah leads the faithful north and finds the city of Zarahemla. Its people left Jerusalem when Zedekiah was taken to Babylon. Their language has changed, and they have no records. Mosiah becomes king of both peoples. Amaleki gives the plates to King Benjamin.

verse.text: Behold, it came to pass that Mosiah discovered that the people of Zarahemla came out from Jerusalem at the time that Zedekiah, king of Judah, was carried away captive into Babylon.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Zedekiah is taken in chains to Babylon.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla cross the sea
routes.text: The Lord brought Mulek’s people across the great waters into the land north.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla go up the Sidon
routes.text: They came from the place of landing up into the south wilderness.

routes.title: Mosiah leads his people down to Zarahemla
routes.text: Mosiah fled out of the land of Nephi and came down into Zarahemla.

routes.title: Zeniff’s people go up to Nephi
routes.text: A group went up into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi.

the-people-of-zarahemla.relatedNote: Omni says Mulek's party left Jerusalem when Zedekiah was taken to Babylon.

mormon-joins-the-records.summary: Mormon, writing centuries later, makes a shorter record from many Nephite records. He finds Nephi's small plates, which hold prophecies of Christ. He adds them to his own record for a wise purpose. He does not know all of it. He recalls King Benjamin's wars against the Lamanites. Holy prophets help Benjamin bring peace to the land.

verse.text: And I do this for a wise purpose; for thus it whispereth me, according to the workings of the Spirit of the Lord which is in me. And now, I do not know all things; but the Lord knoweth all things which are to come; wherefore, he worketh in me to do according to his will.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

the-brother-of-jared-prays.summary: Moroni begins a short version of the Jaredite record, written by the prophet Ether. The Jaredites come from the time of the great tower. Jared asks his brother to pray that their language not be confused. The Lord spares their language and their friends' language. Then the Lord promises to lead them to a choice land. He says he will raise up a great nation from them.

verse.text: And the brother of Jared being a large and mighty man, and a man highly favored of the Lord, Jared, his brother, said unto him: Cry unto the Lord, that he will not confound us that we may not understand our words.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: The LORD confuses the language of all the earth at Babel.

jaredite-kings-and-prophets.summary: Jaredite kings rise and fall as sons rebel against their fathers. Prophets warn that the people will be destroyed if they do not repent. In King Shule's day, the people repent and are blessed. Later, secret bands seek power through murder. A great famine comes, and the people humble themselves. The Lord sends rain, and the land grows fruit again. Prophets keep warning, and many reject them.

verse.text: And it came to pass that when they had humbled themselves sufficiently before the Lord he did send rain upon the face of the earth; and the people began to revive again, and there began to be fruit in the north countries, and in all the countries round about. And the Lord did show forth his power unto them in preserving them from famine.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Omer flees from Moron
routes.text: Omer passed by the hill Shim and Cumorah to a place called Ablom.

the-jaredites-are-destroyed.summary: King Coriantumr fights battle after battle against rival leaders. Shiz takes command after his brother dies. Whole cities and families are destroyed. Coriantumr sees that two million of his people have died, and he grieves. He offers peace, but Shiz refuses. The last armies gather near the hill Ramah. Coriantumr kills Shiz, and he is left alone. Ether finishes his record and hides it.

verse.text: He saw that there had been slain by the sword already nearly two millions of his people, and he began to sorrow in his heart; yea, there had been slain two millions of mighty men, and also their wives and their children.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Coriantumr is later found by the people of Zarahemla.

routes.title: The last Jaredite war
routes.text: The war moved east to the hill Comnor, north to Ripliancum, then to Ramah.

king-benjamins-address.summary: King Benjamin teaches his sons from the records. He chooses his son Mosiah as the next king. Families gather near the temple in Zarahemla and pitch their tents facing it. Benjamin speaks from a tower so all can hear. He says he served them without seeking riches. When they serve others, they are serving God. He warns them not to rebel against God.

verse.text: And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

zeniff-returns-to-nephi.summary: Zeniff wants to settle again in the land of Nephi, where the Nephites first lived. King Laman of the Lamanites lets Zeniff's people have the lands of Nephi and Shilom. They rebuild and farm the land. Later the Lamanites attack to take their crops and flocks. Zeniff's people pray and go out to battle in the Lord's strength. They drive the Lamanites back. Zeniff gives the kingdom to his son Noah.

verse.text: Yea, in the strength of the Lord did we go forth to battle against the Lamanites; for I and my people did cry mightily to the Lord that he would deliver us out of the hands of our enemies, for we were awakened to a remembrance of the deliverance of our fathers.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Zeniff’s people go up to Nephi
routes.text: A group went up into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi.

abinadi-warns-king-noah.summary: King Noah taxes his people heavily to pay for his palaces and wine. He replaces his father's priests with proud ones. The people turn to wickedness. A prophet named Abinadi warns that they will be brought into bondage unless they repent. The people are angry and try to kill him. Noah orders Abinadi brought to him, and Abinadi escapes.

verse.text: And it came to pass that there was a man among them whose name was Abinadi; and he went forth among them, and began to prophesy, saying: Behold, thus saith the Lord, and thus hath he commanded me, saying, Go forth, and say unto this people, thus saith the Lord—Wo be unto this people, for I have seen their abominations, and their wickedness, and their whoredoms; and except they repent I will visit them in mine anger.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Abinadi is later put to death by fire.

waters-of-mormon.summary: Alma, one of Noah's priests, believes Abinadi's words. He teaches them in secret. Believers gather at Mormon, a place with a fountain of pure water. Alma asks if they are willing to bear one another's burdens. He baptizes about two hundred and four people. He ordains priests and teaches them to care for one another. When Noah discovers them, they flee into the wilderness.

verse.text: Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s people flee to Helam
routes.text: Alma’s people fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

noah-falls-and-limhi-rules.summary: A Lamanite army attacks, and King Noah flees, leaving many families behind. His own men later put him to death by fire. Noah's son Limhi becomes king and pays the Lamanites half of all they own. Noah's former priests steal Lamanite daughters, and the Lamanites attack again. Limhi's people try three times to fight free, and they fail. They humble themselves, and the Lord softens the Lamanites' hearts.

verse.text: And now the Lord was slow to hear their cry because of their iniquities; nevertheless the Lord did hear their cries, and began to soften the hearts of the Lamanites that they began to ease their burdens; yet the Lord did not see fit to deliver them out of bondage.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Limhi’s explorers miss Zarahemla
routes.text: Forty-three men looked for Zarahemla. They found a land of bones and returned.

ammon-finds-limhi.summary: King Mosiah sends sixteen men to find Zeniff's people. Ammon leads them to the land of Nephi. He meets King Limhi, Zeniff's grandson, who is glad that Zarahemla still exists. Limhi shows him twenty-four gold plates found among ruins. Ammon says King Mosiah is a seer who can translate them. Gideon proposes giving the Lamanite guards wine. While the guards are drunk, the people escape to Zarahemla.

verse.text: But a seer can know of things which are past, and also of things which are to come, and by them shall all things be revealed, or, rather, shall secret things be made manifest, and hidden things shall come to light, and things which are not known shall be made known by them, and also things shall be made known by them which otherwise could not be known.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Ammon’s men search for Zeniff’s people
routes.text: Sixteen men wandered forty days. They did not know the way up.

routes.title: Limhi’s explorers miss Zarahemla
routes.text: Forty-three men looked for Zarahemla. They found a land of bones and returned.

routes.title: Limhi’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: Limhi’s people went around the land of Shilom toward Zarahemla.

routes.title: A Lamanite army gets lost
routes.text: The army lost the trail. It found Amulon and then Helam.

alma-in-helam.summary: Alma's people settle in a land they call Helam. They ask Alma to be their king, and he refuses. A lost Lamanite army finds them. Amulon, the leader of Noah's former priests, rules over them harshly. He forbids them to pray aloud, so they pray in their hearts. The Lord eases their burdens. Then he puts the guards into a deep sleep, and the people escape to Zarahemla.

verse.text: And I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders, that even you cannot feel them upon your backs, even while you are in bondage; and this will I do that ye may stand as witnesses for me hereafter, and that ye may know of a surety that I, the Lord God, do visit my people in their afflictions.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s people flee to Helam
routes.text: Alma’s people fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

routes.title: A Lamanite army gets lost
routes.text: The army lost the trail. It found Amulon and then Helam.

routes.title: Alma’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: One day to the valley of Alma, then twelve more days to Zarahemla.

the-church-in-zarahemla.summary: Mosiah gathers the people and reads the records of Zeniff's and Alma's groups. The people grieve and rejoice at what they hear. Alma baptizes Limhi's people and sets up churches through the land. Some of the rising generation do not believe. Alma does not know how to judge church members who sin. The Lord tells him to forgive those who repent.

verse.text: Yea, and as often as my people repent will I forgive them their trespasses against me.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-the-younger-converted.summary: Alma's son, also named Alma, works to destroy the church. Four sons of King Mosiah join him. An angel appears to them, and the earth shakes. The angel tells the younger Alma to stop. Alma falls and cannot speak or move for two days. His father and the priests fast and pray. Alma rises and says he has been born of the Spirit. The young men travel to repair the harm they did.

verse.text: For, said he, I have repented of my sins, and have been redeemed of the Lord; behold I am born of the Spirit.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: A voice also stops Saul on the road to Damascus.

judges-replace-the-kings.summary: Mosiah's four sons ask to teach the Lamanites. The Lord tells Mosiah to let them go. Mosiah translates the gold plates found by Limhi's people. None of his sons will be king. Mosiah warns of the harm a wicked king can do. He proposes judges chosen by the voice of the people. The people agree, and the younger Alma becomes the first chief judge.

verse.text: Now it is not common that the voice of the people desireth anything contrary to that which is right; but it is common for the lesser part of the people to desire that which is not right; therefore this shall ye observe and make it your law—to do your business by the voice of the people.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

nehor-and-the-church.summary: Nehor teaches that priests should be paid and that all people will be saved. He kills Gideon, the old man who helped free Limhi's people. Alma, the chief judge, judges him under the law, and he is put to death. Others keep spreading his ideas. Some church members are persecuted. The church's priests work for their own living. The members share their goods with the poor, in the church or out of it.

verse.text: And thus, in their prosperous circumstances, they did not send away any who were naked, or that were hungry, or that were athirst, or that were sick, or that had not been nourished; and they did not set their hearts upon riches; therefore they were liberal to all, both old and young, both bond and free, both male and female, whether out of the church or in the church, having no respect to persons as to those who stood in need.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

amlicis-rebellion.summary: Amlici, a follower of Nehor's ideas, wants to be king. The voice of the people rejects him. His followers make him king anyway and go to war. They join a Lamanite army. Alma leads the Nephites in battle near the river Sidon. He fights Amlici and kills him. The enemy flees into a wilderness of wild beasts.

verse.text: Nevertheless, the Nephites being strengthened by the hand of the Lord, having prayed mightily to him that he would deliver them out of the hands of their enemies, therefore the Lord did hear their cries, and did strengthen them, and the Lamanites and the Amlicites did fall before them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The Amlicite battles
routes.text: The fight moved from Amnihu to Gideon, then back to the river crossing.

alma-preaches-in-zarahemla.summary: Wealth brings pride into the church, and members neglect the poor. Alma gives the judgment seat to Nephihah, a wise elder. He goes out to preach. In Zarahemla he asks if they have been born of God. He asks if they feel a mighty change in their hearts. In Gideon he foretells Christ's birth to Mary and his suffering. He calls the people to repent and be baptized.

verse.text: And now behold, I ask of you, my brethren of the church, have ye spiritually been born of God? Have ye received his image in your countenances? Have ye experienced this mighty change in your hearts?
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Angels announce the Savior's birth in Bethlehem.

routes.title: Alma goes over to Gideon
routes.text: Alma went over to the east of the river Sidon, into the valley of Gideon.

alma-and-amulek-in-ammonihah.summary: The people of Ammonihah reject Alma and throw him out. An angel sends him back. Amulek, a man of the city, takes him in. Together they warn the people and teach of Christ. The lawyer Zeezrom tries to trap them with questions. The people burn the believing women and children and their scriptures. Alma and Amulek are bound and jailed for many days. They pray for strength, the ropes break, and the prison falls.

verse.text: And Alma cried, saying: How long shall we suffer these great afflictions, O Lord? O Lord, give us strength according to our faith which is in Christ, even unto deliverance. And they broke the cords with which they were bound; and when the people saw this, they began to flee, for the fear of destruction had come upon them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
routes.text: Alma went to Melek, then three days north to Ammonihah, then Sidom.

zeezrom-healed.summary: Alma and Amulek find the believers driven from Ammonihah in the land of Sidom. Zeezrom lies sick with a fever because of his sins. He believes in Christ and asks to be healed. Alma prays, and Zeezrom leaps up. Zeezrom is baptized and begins to preach. Then a Lamanite army destroys Ammonihah in one day. The chief captain Zoram rescues the captives, and the church grows.

verse.text: And then Alma cried unto the Lord, saying: O Lord our God, have mercy on this man, and heal him according to his faith which is in Christ.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
routes.text: Alma went to Melek, then three days north to Ammonihah, then Sidom.

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

ammon-serves-king-lamoni.summary: Mosiah's sons go to teach the Lamanites. The Lord tells them to be patient in their trials. Ammon goes to the land of Ishmael and becomes a servant of King Lamoni. Other Lamanites scatter the king's flocks at the water. Ammon defends the flocks alone. Lamoni wonders if Ammon is the Great Spirit. Ammon teaches him about God, the creation, and Christ. Lamoni prays for mercy and falls to the earth.

verse.text: And king Lamoni said: I believe all these things which thou hast spoken. Art thou sent from God?
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The sons of Mosiah go up to Nephi
routes.text: They journeyed many days in the wilderness to reach the land of Nephi.

lamonis-father-believes.summary: Ammon and Lamoni go to free Ammon's brother Aaron from prison in Middoni. On the way they meet Lamoni's father, the king over all the Lamanites. He orders his son to kill Ammon. Ammon defends himself and spares the king's life. The king lets Aaron and the others go free. Aaron later teaches the king about God and redemption. The king offers to give away all his sins to know God. He falls to the earth, and his household believes.

verse.text: O God, Aaron hath told me that there is a God; and if there is a God, and if thou art God, wilt thou make thyself known unto me, and I will give away all my sins to know thee, and that I may be raised from the dead, and be saved at the last day. And now when the king had said these words, he was struck as if he were dead.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla go up the Sidon
routes.text: They came from the place of landing up into the south wilderness.

the-people-bury-their-weapons.summary: The king sends word that the missionaries may teach freely in his lands. Thousands of Lamanites believe. They take the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Other Lamanites prepare to attack them. Their new king, Lamoni's brother, says they once killed many people. They bury their swords deep in the earth and promise never to fight again. When the attackers come, they kneel and pray. Many of the attackers stop and join them.

verse.text: And now it came to pass that when the king had made an end of these sayings, and all the people were assembled together, they took their swords, and all the weapons which were used for the shedding of man's blood, and they did bury them up deep in the earth.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

ammon-rejoices.summary: Ammon recalls their hardships among the Lamanites and the thousands who believed. His brother Aaron warns him against boasting. Ammon says he is nothing in his own strength. In God's strength he can do all things. Alma wishes he were an angel who could call every people to repent. Then he accepts the work God has given him. He rejoices in his brothers' success.

verse.text: Yea, I know that I am nothing; as to my strength I am weak; therefore I will not boast of myself, but I will boast of my God, for in his strength I can do all things; yea, behold, many mighty miracles we have wrought in this land, for which we will praise his name forever.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

the-people-of-ammon.summary: Lamanite attacks threaten the Anti-Nephi-Lehies again. Ammon asks the Lord if they should leave. The Nephites give them the land of Jershon and promise to protect them. They become known as the people of Ammon. They are honest and firm in their faith. A great battle follows, and many families mourn their dead.

verse.text: And they were among the people of Nephi, and also numbered among the people who were of the church of God. And they were also distinguished for their zeal towards God, and also towards men; for they were perfectly honest and upright in all things; and they were firm in the faith of Christ, even unto the end.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Jershon
routes.text: The converted Lamanites left Nephi. The Nephites gave them the land of Jershon.

korihor.summary: Korihor comes to Zarahemla and teaches that no Christ will come. He says people prosper only by their own skill. The people of Gideon bind him and send him to Alma. Korihor demands a sign. Alma says all things show there is a God. Korihor is struck so he cannot speak. He writes that the devil deceived him. He later dies among the Zoramites.

verse.text: But Alma said unto him: Thou hast had signs enough; will ye tempt your God? Will ye say, Show unto me a sign, when ye have the testimony of all these thy brethren, and also all the holy prophets? The scriptures are laid before thee, yea, and all things denote there is a God; yea, even the earth, and all things that are upon the face of it, yea, and its motion, yea, and also all the planets which move in their regular form do witness that there is a Supreme Creator.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alma-among-the-zoramites.summary: The Zoramites are Nephites who have left the church. Alma takes his companions to teach them in Antionum. They see the Zoramites climb a high stand and repeat the same prayer. The prayer thanks God that they are chosen and there will be no Christ. Alma prays for strength to bring them back. Later the Zoramites drive out those who believe. The people of Ammon take them in.

verse.text: Behold, O Lord, their souls are precious, and many of them are our brethren; therefore, give unto us, O Lord, power and wisdom that we may bring these, our brethren, again unto thee.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Melek
routes.text: The people of Ammon left Jershon and came over into the land of Melek.

alma-counsels-corianton.summary: Alma speaks to his son Corianton. Corianton left his mission and went after a harlot named Isabel. His conduct turned the Zoramites away from the message. Alma tells him to repent and forsake his sins. He tells Corianton to go back and repair the harm. He explains why prophets teach of Christ before he comes.

verse.text: Now my son, I would that ye should repent and forsake your sins, and go no more after the lusts of your eyes, but cross yourself in all these things; for except ye do this ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of God. Oh, remember, and take it upon you, and cross yourself in these things.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

moroni-defeats-zerahemnah.summary: The Zoramites join the Lamanites, and Zerahemnah leads an army against the Nephites. Moroni, the young chief captain, gives his men armor and shields. The enemy turns toward Manti. Moroni hides his troops on both sides of the river Sidon. The Nephites fight to defend their families and their freedom. They surround the enemy, and Moroni stops the killing.

verse.text: And again, the Lord has said that: Ye shall defend your families even unto bloodshed. Therefore for this cause were the Nephites contending with the Lamanites, to defend themselves, and their families, and their lands, their country, and their rights, and their religion.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites go “round about” to Manti
routes.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and went round about by the head of Sidon.

routes.title: Moroni marches to Manti
routes.text: Moroni left part of his army in Jershon and marched to the land of Manti.

alma-departs.summary: Alma asks his son Helaman if he believes. Helaman says he does. Alma foretells that the Nephites will one day be destroyed for their sins. He blesses the land and the church. Then Alma leaves for the land of Melek and is never heard of again. Helaman and his brothers set the church in order.

verse.text: Behold, this we know, that he was a righteous man; and the saying went abroad in the church that he was taken up by the Spirit, or buried by the hand of the Lord, even as Moses. But behold, the scriptures saith the Lord took Moses unto himself; and we suppose that he has also received Alma in the spirit, unto himself; therefore, for this cause we know nothing concerning his death and burial.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: No one knows where Moses is buried.

title-of-liberty.summary: Amalickiah wants to be king and draws dissenters to him. Moroni tears his coat and writes on it. He calls the people to defend God, freedom, and families. He raises it on a pole as the title of liberty. The people covenant to defend their rights. Amalickiah flees to the Lamanites. He tricks his way to command of a Lamanite army. His servants kill the Lamanite king, and Amalickiah becomes king.

verse.text: And it came to pass that he rent his coat; and he took a piece thereof, and wrote upon it—In memory of our God, our religion, and freedom, and our peace, our wives, and our children—and he fastened it upon the end of a pole.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

moroni-fortifies-the-cities.summary: Amalickiah stirs up the Lamanites against the Nephites. Moroni builds walls of earth around the cities and towers above them. Mormon says that if all were like Moroni, the devil would have no power. The Lamanites attack Ammonihah and Noah and fail. Moroni strengthens the borders and builds new cities. Teancum stops Morianton's people from fleeing north. Pahoran becomes chief judge.

verse.text: Yea, verily, verily I say unto you, if all men had been, and were, and ever would be, like unto Moroni, behold, the very powers of hell would have been shaken forever; yea, the devil would never have power over the hearts of the children of men.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

routes.title: Morianton flees toward the land northward
routes.text: Morianton’s people fled toward the land northward. They were stopped by the narrow pass.

routes.title: Teancum heads off Morianton
routes.text: Moroni sent an army to head off Morianton. They met him at the pass.

teancum-kills-amalickiah.summary: King-men want a king and refuse to defend the land. Moroni forces them to fight or be put down. Amalickiah takes the cities along the east sea. At night Teancum slips into his tent and kills him. Amalickiah's brother Ammoron becomes king. Moroni and Teancum draw the Lamanites out of the city of Mulek. They surround the army and take the city.

verse.text: And it came to pass that Teancum stole privily into the tent of the king, and put a javelin to his heart; and he did cause the death of the king immediately that he did not awake his servants.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
routes.text: Amalickiah took city after city on the east borders by the seashore.

routes.title: Teancum draws the Lamanites out of Mulek
routes.text: The Lamanites chased Teancum down by the seashore until they came near Bountiful.

the-two-thousand-young-men.summary: The people of Ammon think of breaking their promise never to fight. Helaman persuades them not to. Two thousand of their sons, who made no such promise, enlist. They choose Helaman to lead them. Their mothers taught them that God would deliver them if they did not doubt. They fight to defend their families and take the cities of Cumeni and Manti. Many are wounded, but none of them dies.

verse.text: Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Helaman’s young men march to Judea
routes.text: Helaman marched the two thousand young men to the city of Judea.

routes.title: Helaman lures the army out of Antiparah
routes.text: They marched near Antiparah as if going to the city by the seashore.

moroni-frees-the-prisoners.summary: Ammoron offers to trade prisoners. Moroni demands that the Lamanites also leave the land, and Ammoron refuses. Moroni finds a Lamanite servant among his men. The man carries wine to the guards at the city of Gid. While the guards sleep, the Nephites pass weapons to the prisoners. Moroni takes the city without killing the sleeping guards.

verse.text: But behold, this was not the desire of Moroni; he did not delight in murder or bloodshed, but he delighted in the saving of his people from destruction; and for this cause he might not bring upon him injustice, he would not fall upon the Lamanites and destroy them in their drunkenness.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

moroni-and-pahoran.summary: The city of Nephihah falls because no help comes. Moroni writes an angry letter to Pahoran, the chief judge. He accuses the government of neglecting the armies. Pahoran answers that king-men have driven him out of Zarahemla. He says he is not angry. Moroni joins Pahoran and defeats the king-men. They retake the cities, and Teancum dies after killing Ammoron. Peace returns to the land.

verse.text: And now, in your epistle you have censured me, but it mattereth not; I am not angry, but do rejoice in the greatness of your heart. I, Pahoran, do not seek for power, save only to retain my judgment-seat that I may preserve the rights and the liberty of my people. My soul standeth fast in that liberty in the which God hath made us free.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Moroni retakes the east coast
routes.text: The Lamanites fled from city to city, then down to the seashore and Moroni.

hagoths-ships.summary: Helaman dies, and his brother Shiblon receives the records. Many people move into the land northward. Hagoth builds a large ship by the west sea. Many sail away, and some are never heard of again. Moroni dies. Shiblon gives the records to Helaman's son, also named Helaman.

verse.text: And it came to pass that Hagoth, he being an exceedingly curious man, therefore he went forth and built him an exceedingly large ship, on the borders of the land Bountiful, by the land Desolation, and launched it forth into the west sea, by the narrow neck which led into the land northward.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Hagoth’s ships sail north
routes.text: Hagoth launched ships into the west sea. Some went to the land northward.

routes.title: Nephites spread into the land northward
routes.text: Many people went forth unto the land northward and spread out.

kishkumen-and-coriantumr.summary: Three sons of Pahoran compete for the judgment seat after his death. The voice of the people chooses Pahoran, his son. A hired killer named Kishkumen murders him on the judgment seat. Kishkumen's band swears to keep his secret. Coriantumr, a Nephite who joined the Lamanites, marches into Zarahemla and takes it. Moronihah and Lehi surround his army, and the Nephites retake the city.

verse.text: Now when those people who were desirous that he should be their governor saw that he was condemned unto death, therefore they were angry, and behold, they sent forth one Kishkumen, even to the judgment-seat of Pahoran, and murdered Pahoran as he sat upon the judgment-seat.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Coriantumr strikes the center
routes.text: A Lamanite army came into the center of the land and took Zarahemla.

the-church-grows-in-peace.summary: Many people move into the land northward. Where trees are few, they build houses of cement. Tens of thousands join the church in a time of peace. The humble fast and pray often and grow firmer in their faith. Others grow proud. Helaman dies, and his son Nephi becomes chief judge.

verse.text: Nevertheless they did fast and pray oft, and did wax stronger and stronger in their humility, and firmer and firmer in the faith of Christ, unto the filling their souls with joy and consolation, yea, even to the purifying and the sanctification of their hearts, which sanctification cometh because of their yielding their hearts unto God.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Hagoth’s ships sail north
routes.text: Hagoth launched ships into the west sea. Some went to the land northward.

routes.title: Nephites spread into the land northward
routes.text: Many people went forth unto the land northward and spread out.

nephites-lose-the-south.summary: Nephite dissenters join the Lamanites in war. The Nephites are driven back to the land of Bountiful. Moronihah wins back about half the land. The Nephites see that their pride and wickedness have made them weak. They had boasted in their own strength. So they were left to their own strength and lost almost all their lands.

verse.text: And because of this their great wickedness, and their boastings in their own strength, they were left in their own strength; therefore they did not prosper, but were afflicted and smitten, and driven before the Lamanites, until they had lost possession of almost all their lands.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Nephites driven into Bountiful
routes.text: The Nephites were driven into the land of Bountiful and fortified a line.

nephi-and-lehi-in-prison.summary: Nephi gives up the judgment seat to preach with his brother Lehi. They remember their father's words to build on the rock of Christ. They preach from Bountiful to Zarahemla and on to the land of Nephi. Lamanites put them in prison. A pillar of fire surrounds them, and the walls shake. A still, quiet voice calls the people to repent. About three hundred people see this and believe.

verse.text: And it came to pass when they heard this voice, and beheld that it was not a voice of thunder, neither was it a voice of a great tumultuous noise, but behold, it was a still voice of perfect mildness, as if it had been a whisper, and it did pierce even to the very soul—
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Nephi and Lehi preach from Bountiful
routes.text: They began at Bountiful, then Gid and Mulek, then Zarahemla and Nephi.

the-gadianton-robbers-spread.summary: The Lamanites become more righteous than the Nephites. Many Lamanites come to teach the Nephites. The two peoples trade and travel freely. Then murders and secret bands spread among the Nephites. Those bands are the robbers of Gadianton. The Lamanites hunt down the robbers in their land. The Nephites support them until the robbers fill the land.

verse.text: And it came to pass on the other hand, that the Nephites did build them up and support them, beginning at the more wicked part of them, until they had overspread all the land of the Nephites, and had seduced the more part of the righteous until they had come down to believe in their works and partake of their spoils, and to join with them in their secret murders and combinations.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla cross the sea
routes.text: The Lord brought Mulek’s people across the great waters into the land north.

nephi-on-his-garden-tower.summary: Nephi returns from the north and finds the robbers ruling in Zarahemla. He prays on the tower in his garden near the highway. Men passing by hear him and call others. A crowd gathers to learn why he mourns. Nephi calls them to repent. He warns that they will be destroyed if they do not.

verse.text: And it came to pass that there were certain men passing by and saw Nephi as he was pouring out his soul unto God upon the tower; and they ran and told the people what they had seen, and the people came together in multitudes that they might know the cause of so great mourning for the wickedness of the people.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

samuel-the-lamanite.summary: Samuel, a Lamanite prophet, preaches in Zarahemla, and the people cast him out. The Lord tells him to return. They will not let him into the city, so he climbs the wall. He warns of destruction within four hundred years unless they repent. He says they reject prophets and love their riches. He says they have sought happiness in doing wrong.

verse.text: And it came to pass that they would not suffer that he should enter into the city; therefore he went and got upon the wall thereof, and stretched forth his hand and cried with a loud voice, and prophesied unto the people whatsoever things the Lord put into his heart.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Samuel foretells a night without darkness at Christ's birth.

the-sign-of-christs-birth.summary: Unbelievers set a day to kill those who wait for Samuel's sign. Nephi, the son of Nephi, prays all day for his people. The Lord tells him the sign will come that night. At sunset there is no darkness. The night stays light as day, and a new star appears. Many believe and are baptized.

verse.text: And it came to pass that the words which came unto Nephi were fulfilled, according as they had been spoken; for behold, at the going down of the sun there was no darkness; and the people began to be astonished because there was no darkness when the night came.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Angels announce the Savior's birth in Bethlehem.

lachoneus-gathers-the-people.summary: The people begin to forget the signs. Robber bands grow strong and attack Nephites and Lamanites alike. The robbers' leader Giddianhi writes to demand that Lachoneus surrender. Lachoneus, the governor, refuses and has the people pray for strength. He gathers them in one place with their flocks and seven years of food. The robbers find nothing to eat and attack. Giddianhi dies, and his army is defeated. The people give thanks for their deliverance.

verse.text: Now behold, this Lachoneus, the governor, was a just man, and could not be frightened by the demands and the threatenings of a robber; therefore he did not hearken to the epistle of Giddianhi, the governor of the robbers, but he did cause that his people should cry unto the Lord for strength against the time that the robbers should come down against them.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: People gather from the south
routes.text: The people came from all parts of the land into one place.

routes.title: People gather from the north
routes.text: People in the land northward also came to the gathering place.

pride-breaks-the-church.summary: The people return to their lands and grow rich. Some grow proud, and the people split into ranks. The church is broken up except among a few Lamanites. Some judges secretly put to death prophets who testify of Christ. Their friends plan to destroy the governor and set up a king.

verse.text: And thus there became a great inequality in all the land, insomuch that the church began to be broken up; yea, insomuch that in the thirtieth year the church was broken up in all the land save it were among a few of the Lamanites who were converted unto the true faith; and they would not depart from it, for they were firm, and steadfast, and immovable, willing with all diligence to keep the commandments of the Lord.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

storm-at-christs-death.summary: In the thirty-fourth year, a great storm arises. Zarahemla burns, and the city of Moroni sinks into the sea. Earth covers the city of Moronihah. Thick darkness lies on the land for three days. The survivors hear a voice name the cities that were destroyed. The speaker says he is Jesus Christ. He asks for a broken heart and a contrite spirit.

verse.text: And ye shall offer for a sacrifice unto me a broken heart and a contrite spirit. And whoso cometh unto me with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, him will I baptize with fire and with the Holy Ghost, even as the Lamanites, because of their faith in me at the time of their conversion, were baptized with fire and with the Holy Ghost, and they knew it not.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Darkness covers the land at the crucifixion.

jesus-appears-at-bountiful.summary: About 2,500 people gather near the temple in Bountiful. They hear a voice, and the Father introduces his beloved Son. Jesus comes down from heaven in a white robe. He invites them to feel the wounds in his hands, feet, and side. They fall down and worship him. He gives Nephi and others power to baptize. He teaches them to baptize without disputes.

verse.text: Arise and come forth unto me, that ye may thrust your hands into my side, and also that ye may feel the prints of the nails in my hands and in my feet, that ye may know that I am the God of Israel, and the God of the whole earth, and have been slain for the sins of the world.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Jesus invites Thomas to touch his wounds.

two-centuries-of-peace.summary: After Christ's visit, all the people join the church. They share their goods and have no rich or poor. There are no Lamanites or other divisions. There is no contention, because the love of God is in their hearts. After about two hundred years, pride returns. People build separate churches and form classes again. The record keeper Ammaron hides the sacred records.

verse.text: And it came to pass that there was no contention in the land, because of the love of God which did dwell in the hearts of the people.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

mormon-as-a-young-man.summary: Ammaron tells Mormon, about ten years old, where the records are hidden. At fifteen, Mormon is visited by the Lord. War begins near the river Sidon. At sixteen, Mormon leads the Nephite armies. The Nephites lose city after city. Their sorrow does not lead them to repent. A treaty gives them the land northward.

verse.text: And I, being fifteen years of age and being somewhat of a sober mind, therefore I was visited of the Lord, and tasted and knew of the goodness of Jesus.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Mormon’s army leaves the land southward
routes.text: The Nephites lost Angola and David. They moved to Joshua, then fled north.

mormon-refuses-revenge.summary: Mormon fortifies the land of Desolation. The Nephites win battles, then boast and swear to take revenge. Mormon refuses to lead them for that purpose. The Nephites attack and are driven back. Both peoples grow more cruel. Mormon takes the records from the hill Shim. He agrees to lead the army again, without hope.

verse.text: Behold, I had led them, notwithstanding their wickedness I had led them many times to battle, and had loved them, according to the love of God which was in me, with all my heart; and my soul had been poured out in prayer unto my God all the day long for them; nevertheless, it was without faith, because of the hardness of their hearts.
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

routes.title: Lamanites cross the neck
routes.text: The Lamanites came down to the city of Desolation to battle.

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.

the-last-battle-at-cumorah.summary: Mormon gathers the Nephites in the land of Cumorah. He hides the records in the hill but gives some plates to his son Moroni. The Lamanites attack, and the Nephite armies are destroyed. Mormon mourns for the people who would not repent. Moroni later writes that his father was killed. He is left alone to finish the record. He writes that it will come forth in a later day.

verse.text: O ye fair ones, how could ye have departed from the ways of the Lord! O ye fair ones, how could ye have rejected that Jesus, who stood with open arms to receive you!
verse.translation: Text of the 1981 edition with 2013 corrections, via bcbooks/scriptures-json (bom-4)

alsoRead.note: Joseph Smith speaks of glad tidings from Cumorah.

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.
